_about: What the Switch Configurator offers from the bus. Tunables only: no code holds a device list. `kinds` is matched (case-insensitive substring) against each discovered thing's protocols, scanner kind and device_class (APKSoftapp.discovered). `fields` names, in order of preference, the leaf a scanner publishes a value under (empty: nothing on the bench publishes one, see _measured); the SNMP bridge (PLUGIN.SNMP bridge.rs) publishes every OID it walks as a leaf with '_' for '.', and `port_count` beside `_describe`: the rows of the MIB's port table (ROAD-3518). FALLBACK ONLY: an optional `portRows` lists table columns whose rows are the front-panel ports, counted (distinct <column>_<index> leaves) only when no `fields.portCount` leaf is on the bus; it is absent because PLUGIN.SNMP says port_count itself. A switch with neither keeps the editor's port count.
_measured: Bench broker 2026-11-04 (ROAD-3502, ROAD-3518): one switch, snmp/Device/snmp_00_14_d1_1e_a0_5f (device_class 'Network Switch', model 'TEG-240WS  3.02.03'). PLUGIN.SNMP walks only its MIB's own subtree (rootOid 1.3.6.1.4.1.28866.2.11, mib_file TEG-240WS-MIB), so NO MIB-II leaf is on the bus: sysName, sysDescr, sysLocation and ifNumber never appear, and the enterprise MIB has no name, description or location object. Name and model come from the thing itself (its MAC and its runner's model leaf). The port count is …/snmp/Device/snmp_00_14_d1_1e_a0_5f/port_count = 24: PLUGIN.SNMP counts the rows of the table its MIB indexes by ifIndex (TEG-240WS configPortTable; ifNumber would also have counted the VLAN and CPU interfaces). netgear and trendnet plugins are online but publish no Device/ tree on the bench.
